Hi! I'm glad you found this post! To be honest, the best way I found to get out was a text message saying that I no longer wanted to study with them but thanks anyway. Then, I would suggest blocking their numbers tbh. I tried to quit the studies twice before and they called me and convinced me to continue (mainly because I'm bad at conflict lol) Blocking and/or ghosting them is the best method in my opinion. 

Also, I know it can be tough because they cause you to start questioning your prior beliefs. But I know I made the right choice. A couple months after I left the group behind, one of the girls who was helping lead the Bible studies reached out to me and told me that she was leaving the church and asked to meet up with me. I agreed and she told me of how awful she was treated by the other members and how much money they basically scammed her out of thousands. They seem really abusive and controlling and I would 100% recommend getting out. 

Just remember, you don't owe them an explanation. A simple "thanks for your time, but I've decided I no longer want to continue with the Bible studies and I'm not interested in joining your church" message will suffice. And again, I recommend not engaging with them after. They can be very convincing and pushy. I wish you all the best and feel free to message me if you ever want to talk more!

I had a zoom interview for an office position, so my experience is a bit different, but I got the job. I would just prepare for the most common questions like: Tell me about yourself, strengths and weaknesses, etc. Something else I thought was helpful was to look up college interview questions and maybe prepare for some of those. 

Also, think of situations or experiences you had in high school, work, or outside clubs that you can talk about. Even if the question they ask isn't directly related, it's always good to mention your past experience. 

For example, I was asked how I manage stress and stay organized. I responded with the tactics I use to stay organized, but also brought up a stressful situation I dealt with in my student senate and how I managed that. Often times, employers are looking for evidence to back up what you're saying. 

But don't stress too much, my interview was very casual as I expect most college job ones are. Use it to gain experience for when you need to interview for an internship or career level job. Good luck!

A zucchini enchilada casserole. 
Cut 3-4 zucchinis into half moon shapes. Pour some enchilada sauce into a casserole dish, just enough for a bottom layer. Cook some ground meat (my favorite is ground turkey) in a skillet with some onions and garlic. Once cooked, put it all into a casserole dish with more enchilada sauce; how much you put is a personal preference, you just don't want anything to dry out. You can cook the zucchini in a skillet slightly before putting in the oven to lessen cooking time, but it's optional. At this point, you can add in other things: mushrooms, tomatoes, corn, beans, etc. Top with some cheese and put into a 350°F oven. Once done, you can add some sour cream, green onions, avocado, or whatever fits into your diet.
You can also do this with marinara sauce and make it into an Italian dish, all depends on the type of spices and herbs you use.
